### 🟡 Changes recommended Contentless candidates now produce artificial empty output messages instead of being omitted.
1 open issue - [Avoid emitting empty messages for contentless candidates](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-genai/pull/908#discussion_r4299827487) · New
What changed in this PR Fixes Google GenAI streaming telemetry to report one output message per candidate rather than per chunk. **Changes:** - Merges candidates by index, joining adjacent text while preserving part order and the latest finish reason. - Adds merge tests and shared sync/async streaming coverage. - Records the fix in the changelog. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | instrumentation/​opentelemetry-instrumentation-google-genai/​tests/​generate_content/​test_merge_streamed_candidates.py | Tests merging and chunk immutability. | | instrumentation/​opentelemetry-instrumentation-google-genai/​tests/​generate_content/​streaming_base.py | Adds sync/async output-message regression coverage. | | instrumentation/​opentelemetry-instrumentation-google-genai/​src/​opentelemetry/​instrumentation/​google_genai/​generate_content.py | Merges candidates before generating streamed output messages. | | instrumentation/​opentelemetry-instrumentation-google-genai/​.changelog/​908.fixed | Documents the streaming correction. |
Review effort: Balanced

Looks good to me, thanks @pcbeingused333.

Left one small suggestion around ordering.

review_comments.body: Creating `Content(parts=[])` unconditionally turns a candidate whose chunks all have `content=None` (for example, a blocked response) into an empty output message. `to_output_messages()` skips contentless candidates, so this changes existing behavior and differs from non-streamed responses. Leave merged content unset until a chunk supplies content, and add a regression test confirming that an entirely contentless candidate produces no output message in both streaming variants.

This will return the items in the order they were received, no necessarily their index order. We could do something like this to guarantee the order:

```suggestion
    return [merged[index] for index in sorted(merged)]
```
Done in c1d17e0, merged candidates now come back sorted by index, with a test where index 1 streams first.
